主要内容: Intel (INTC) reported its Q1 2022 earnings, beating both the top and bottom lines. However, the company issued weaker-than-expected guidance for its fiscal second quarter. The PC chip business performed below expectations, partly due to Apple's shift to its own chips. Revenue for the quarter was $18.35 billion, slightly above analyst estimates, but down 7% year-over-year. The gross margin narrowed to 50.4% from 55.2%. The Client Computing Group, which includes PC chips, generated $9.29 billion in revenue, down 13% from the $9.42 billion consensus. Intel also announced a new segment, Datacenter and AI, which saw a 22% revenue increase to $6.03 billion. The company delayed the release of its server chip, Granite Rapids, to 2024 and announced plans to acquire Tower Semiconductor and build chip factories in Germany and Ohio. Intel's CEO, Pat Gelsinger, warned of continued industry challenges until at least 2024. Intel reported Q1 2022 earnings of 70 cents per share and $18.0 billion in revenue. Analysts had expected 83 cents in adjusted earnings per share on $18.38 billion in revenue. For the full fiscal year, Intel raised its adjusted earnings guidance by 10 cents to $3.60 per share on $76 billion in revenue, exceeding the $3.50 per share and $75.78 billion in revenue forecast. Zinsner noted that inventory challenges will persist in the second quarter but ease in the second half of the year. He also mentioned that China's lockdowns are increasing supply fears, and inflation could reduce the PC market for the full year. Intel aims to launch its server chips codenamed Sapphire Rapids "meaningfully faster" than its Ice Lake chips, which became available in 2019. Gelsinger stated that all hyper-scale data center companies are interested in these chips. Despite the after-hours move, Intel shares have fallen about 9% since the start of 2021, while the S&P 500 is down about 10% over the same period.
